{"id":"persona-5s4b.79","title":"GPG attestor uses the last subkey fingerprint as the identity instead of the primary key fingerprint","description":"persona-attestors/src/gpg.rs:253-283 parse_gpg_colons() tracks a single current_fp and overwrites it on every fpr record:

    Some(&"fpr") => { current_fp = fields.get(9).map(|s| s.to_string()); }

but gpg --with-colons emits an fpr record after every sub record as well as after each pub. Verified against real output from `gpg --batch --no-tty --list-keys --with-colons --fingerprint` on this machine:

    pub:-:1024:17:0FCDD8E5035D6B1D:...
    fpr:::::::::677AB7B4A1EC7CD7C15B04810FCDD8E5035D6B1D:   <- primary
    uid:-::::...
    sub:-:4096:16:57D0B2691725ABC2:...
    fpr:::::::::C97922CD569356C21C0BADB357D0B2691725ABC2:   <- subkey, overwrites current_fp
    pub:... (next key -> flush)

Trigger: any GPG key that has at least one subkey -- which is essentially every real-world key, since gpg --gen-key creates an encryption subkey by default.

What goes wrong: the flush at gpg.rs:263 (on the next pub) and at gpg.rs:279 (end of output) pairs the primary keys uid with the LAST subkeys fingerprint. make_claim (gpg.rs:285-298) takes the last 8 hex chars of that, so the emitted identity for the key above is spiffe://ssh.local/gpg/1725abc2 (subkey 57D0B2691725ABC2) instead of spiffe://ssh.local/gpg/035d6b1d (primary 0FCDD8E5035D6B1D).

Consequences: (a) the SPIFFE ID does not identify the key the user thinks it does and cannot be cross-referenced against a published primary fingerprint; (b) the identity is unstable -- adding, rotating or expiring an encryption subkey silently changes the users SPIFFE ID, invalidating any relying-party enrollment keyed on it; (c) with multiple subkeys the result depends on gpg output ordering.

The unit test at gpg.rs:355-366 passes only because its fixture contains no sub record, so the suite gives false confidence. A regression test needs a fixture with subkeys.

Fix direction: capture the fpr that immediately follows a pub and ignore fpr records that follow a sub (track which record type was last seen), and flush on pub rather than relying on both current_fp and current_uid being Some.","status":"open","priority":0,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:59:50.103399808Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-13T20:59:50.103399808Z","labels":["correctness","review"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-5s4b.79","depends_on_id":"persona-5s4b","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:59:50.126100109Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}

new_value: Fixed in 1a8e749: --list-secret-keys replaces --list-keys (parser retargeted pub/sub -> sec/ssb), the fpr following sec names the identity instead of the last subkey's, and the SPIFFE path carries the full fingerprint (did:key the full SHA-256). Fixtures are real gpg output from throwaway keys. Verified on the real keyring: strangers' keys gone, 15 candidates, all full 40-hex.
